## Outcomes for `sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec`

The candidates come from the spec's requirements. Each line says what you get. The **Spec** column cites the source, so the roadmap never repeats requirement text. The list is **not ranked**: the ranking is yours.

| # | Outcome | Spec | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A Parquet filing-index catalog for a chosen range of archived quarters, built from the SEC quarterly master indexes, with each row's source recorded | R1, R3, R5; §2.1 Backfill, §4.2, §4.4, §4.5 row contract, §4.6 | Requests are few: 4 quarterly files a year, so about 130 since 1993. At 3 req/s that is under a minute of request time. File size and parse time are unknown until a real quarter is loaded. |
| O2 | New daily indexes added to the catalog, catching up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries, with overlap against the baseline deduplicated | R2, R5; §4.2 Daily, §4.4 Open quarter | About 250 daily files a year. Listing and download take seconds a day at 3 req/s. |
| O3 | The catalog rebuilt from stored original bytes after a parser or schema change, with no SEC download and no duplicate records | R6; §4.3 Validation, §4.6 Transform | No SEC traffic. Storage is about 1× the raw index volume, the same unknown as in O1. |
| O4 | Quarterly re-reads that apply additions and field changes, and remove a closed quarter's records only after an approval tied to that file's hash | R7, R10; §4.2 Reconciliation, §4.4 Closed quarter / Changes | Re-reads every supported quarter weekly, about 130 requests per run, under a minute of requests. |
| O5 | Readers only ever see complete quarters, resolved through one active pointer per quarter. A crashed or conflicting run leaves the previous quarter readable. | R9; §4.6 Publish, §5 Guarantees | Small. |
| O6 | One shared SEC request budget at 3 req/s with an identifying User-Agent, across backfill, daily and reconciliation, with bounded retries and a halt on access denial | R8, R11; §4.3, §4.8 HTTP/SEC rows, §5 | Small. Waiting for the lease adds wall-clock time when runs overlap. |
| O7 | Unattended operation on Azure: Data Factory runs Container Apps jobs daily at 05:00 ET and weekly reconciliation on Sundays, with storage in ADLS and Table Storage and production identities | R4, R11; §4.1, §4.8, §4.9, §7 Phase 2 | Azure spend can't be estimated until a run is measured. Setting up the infrastructure-as-code, identities and pipelines takes a material amount of your time. |

Qualities to place when the roadmap is written: manifests, traceability, full validation suite, monitoring and alerts, runbooks.

## Track

**A — SEC filing-index catalog (known progression).** I propose one track. Each outcome extends or protects the same catalog, and none stands without O1. O7 hosts the same commands rather than answering a separate question. Split it off if you'd rather run the catalog locally with its own ranking.

## Choices already made
- **Language and tooling:** Python 3.14 (`.python-version`) in a uv workspace.
- **Package layout:** the repo has four scaffold packages (client, download, index-ingest, ingest), while spec §4.9 puts all the code in `sec-edgar-ingest`. That mapping is left to each piece of work's own session.
- **Platform:** Azure, per R4. Both the ADR and the spec are still marked **Proposed**, and §7 step 1 asks for them to be accepted. I've recorded R4 as the intended platform, not as an accepted one.

The roadmap will be written to `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`.

## Request
**Please rank O1–O7, and confirm the single track and its kind, or split it.**

Optionally, I can also fetch one real quarterly `master.idx`, using your SEC User-Agent, to measure its size and parse time. That would firm up the O1 and O3 cost notes. Tell me alongside your ranking if you want that.
